Knowledge has been accumulated up to this point, and every kind of good hypothesis leads to virtue immediately, and from good deeds, someone boasts greatly, but if someone opposes this and despises the holy and divine Scripture, which is composed in the Hebrew language, they would say that it is written in a certain language, and thus, one would contemptuously dismiss the other languages, including Greek, and number them among the less esteemed, and it is said that the tower of Babel was divided into many languages by God's power, and the Greeks would not have their language as a discovery of piety, but rather as one of the languages that were divided

For they thought, according to the eloquence, of the wise, as it is credible, they considered themselves inventors of eloquence and ascribed to themselves the works of ineffable power, but blessed David curses them, saying the Lord will destroy all deceitful lips and tongues, which say we will magnify our tongue, our lips are our own, and they claim to be the inventors of eloquence, but the Lord gave tongues divinely, and each has their own unique sound, and the Attic dialect is praised for its sweet sound, but this is not relevant to the cultivators of sanctimony and right living, and it is not useful to them

Men are accustomed to eagerly singing, sometimes rebuking those who are in vices and leading a life bound by crimes, but they praise those who are skilled in music and those who are accustomed to flattering the wealthy; however, if they are alien to right studies, anyone will rightly rebuke them; but those who spend their life in the laws of God, even if they are not eloquent, are loved by God; for what is esteemed is not eloquence, but virtue, and those who are educated in sacred letters, even if they are not eloquent, are pleasing to God; and it is not right to despise them because they lack eloquence, for what is important is not eloquence, but the love of God

Having renounced all other virtue, we have been taught every kind of inspired virtue from the sacred scriptures, and we know someone who is familiar with the scriptures and the utmost glory of virtue; one should teach, whether you marvel at the books of the Greeks or the doctrine of the Hebrews; we have submitted to the preaching of dogma; for the sacred scriptures are a gift from God, and we use the language of the Greeks, which is a kind of preliminary exercise; all wisdom and every word come from the Lord

He attempts to help the Greek brotherhoods in another way, saying Asclepius heals our bodies, the Muses educate our minds with Asclepius, Apollo, and Mercury, while Ares and Enyo are allies in war, and Vulcan assigns and divides the arts, and all these things are moderated by Pallas with Jupiter, a virgin without a mother, and asks if they surpass us in these individual things, in arts, counsel, and wisdom, whether in useful or imitative arts, such as statuary, painting, economics, medicine, which comes from Asclepius, whose temples are everywhere on earth, and God allows us to enjoy them continually

For Asclepius has often healed me, the one who is sick, by indicating remedies, and Zeus is a witness of these things, and if we have committed ourselves to the spirit of desertion, we have better things concerning the soul, and body, and external goods, having left these things, for what reason do you turn to those things?
pass_b_english: …Knowledge has been accumulated up to this point, and every kind of good hypothesis leads to virtue immediately, and from good deeds, someone boasts greatly.

But if someone opposes this and despises the holy and divine Scripture, which is composed in the Hebrew language, they would say that it is written in a certain language, even as they mock the Scripture.

Moreover, if one were to contemptuously dismiss the other languages, including Greek, and number them among the less esteemed, it would be akin to saying that the Greeks do not have their language as a discovery of piety, but rather as one of the languages that were divided by God's power, as in the story of the tower of Babel, where the languages were divided into many tongues.
The wise, as it is credible, thought that they were the inventors of eloquence, and they ascribed the works of ineffable power to themselves.

But blessed David curses them, saying: 'The Lord will destroy all deceitful lips and the tongue that speaks great things, which say, Our tongue is our own, we are the inventors of eloquence' (Psalm 12:3-4).
The Lord gave tongues divinely, and each has its own unique sound.
The Attic dialect is praised for its sweet sound, but this is not relevant to the cultivators of sanctimony and right living, and it is not useful to them.

Men are accustomed to eagerly singing, sometimes rebuking those who are caught up in vices and leading a life bound by crimes, but they praise those who are skilled in music and those who are accustomed to playing the flute and those who are lovers of the wealthy.
On the other hand, those who spend their lives in the service of God's laws, even if they are not eloquent, are loved by God.
In fact, what is truly esteemed is not eloquence, but virtue.
This is evident in the case of those who are educated in sacred letters, for even if they are not eloquent, they are still pleasing to God.
We have been taught every kind of inspired virtue from the sacred scriptures, having renounced all other virtue.
The scriptures, which are a gift from God, have provided us with a thorough understanding of virtue and its utmost glory, which is worthy of wonder.
We use the language of the Greeks, which is a kind of preliminary exercise, and we have submitted to the preaching of dogma.
All wisdom and every word come from the Lord (Ecclesiasticus 1:4).

In an effort to support the Greek brotherhoods, he offers an alternative perspective, suggesting that Asclepius heals our physical bodies, while the Muses, together with Asclepius, Apollo, and Mercury, educate our minds.
On the other hand, Ares and Enyo are allies in the midst of war.
Furthermore, Vulcan is responsible for assigning and dividing the various arts, all of which are overseen by Pallas, a virgin without a mother, who works in conjunction with Jupiter.

He then inquires as to whether they surpass us in these individual areas, including the arts, counsel, and wisdom, regardless of whether these arts are practical or imitative, such as statuary, painting, economics, or medicine, which originates from Asclepius and is available to us everywhere on earth, allowing us to continually enjoy the benefits that God provides.
Asclepius, the renowned healer, has often restored my health by prescribing remedies, and Zeus himself bears witness to these events.

If we have surrendered ourselves to the spirit of desertion, we possess better things, namely, the well-being of our souls, bodies, and external goods, having left these things, for what reason do you turn back to … those things?
